title: Mental addition & subtraction
examples: Can you show me how to add 8 and 5 quickly?
What is a good trick for adding numbers close to ten?
Can you explain the compensation method with an example?

explain.say: Today we learn quick math tricks for adding and subtracting.

items: Find the number to make ten.
Add that amount to the other number.

Next we try near doubles, like adding eight and nine.

explain.say: In real life, you use these tricks when counting money.

faq.a: It means finding the small number needed to reach the next ten. For example, if you have 8, you need 2 to make 10.
asks: How do I get to ten quickly?
What is the trick for making ten?

faq.q: When should I use near doubles?
faq.a: You use this when the two numbers you add are very close to being the same. It is faster than adding them straight away.
asks: What if the numbers are far apart?

faq.a: Compensation means making the numbers easier to work with first. You change them slightly and then adjust your answer.
asks: Can I use it for subtraction too?

faq.q: Do I have to use these tricks all the time?
faq.a: No, you can use any method you know. These tricks are just ways to make your brain work faster.
asks: Is there a right way to add?
When should I just count my fingers?

faq.q: Which trick is best for big numbers?
faq.a: For very large numbers, compensation by rounding to the nearest hundred can be very helpful. It keeps the calculation simple.
asks: Which trick is for big numbers?
Is there a trick for hundreds?

facts: Bridging ten helps you add numbers that are close to a multiple of ten.
Near doubles means adding two numbers that are almost equal.
Compensation involves rounding numbers to make addition easier.
These tricks help build mental math fluency for quick answers.

quiz.say: What is the best way to calculate 9 plus 7 using bridging ten?
quiz.why: You see that 9 needs 1 to make 10. Then you take the remaining 6 and add it to 10, which makes 16.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you subtracted the missing one from the 7 instead of adding it.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you added 1 to 9 and then added 7 to the 1, which is counting too much.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only added 1 to 9, but you forgot to add the rest of the 7.

quiz.say: If you calculate 11 plus 12 using near doubles, what is the answer?
quiz.why: You can think of 11 plus 11, which is 22. Then you add the extra 1 to get 23.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you only added the extra 1 to the first number, not the second.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you subtracted 1 from both numbers instead of adding them.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only added the numbers to get the double, forgetting the last one.

quiz.say: To calculate 18 plus 24 using compensation, what is the result?
quiz.why: You can round 18 up to 20, and 24 up to 25. Then 20 plus 25 is 45. But you added 2 too much, so you subtract 2 from 45 to get 43. Wait, let's try rounding to the nearest ten: 20 plus 20 is 40. Then 2 more plus 4 more is 6. So 40 plus 6 is 46. Let's re-evaluate: 18 is 2 less than 20. 24 is 1 more than 23. wrong.0: This is wrong because you only added the tens digits and forgot the ones digits.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you added 20 plus 20 and then added 6, which is not how compensation works.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you incorrectly adjusted the numbers by rounding both down to the nearest ten.
